0.title: God's Good Design for Body and Desire
0.overview:
Few subjects are more confusing or painful in our culture than sexuality. The modern West tells people that their sexual desires define who they are, that consent is the only moral boundary and that any limit on sexual expression is oppressive. Many Christians, meanwhile, have heard the church speak about sex mainly in terms of rules and shame, or not at all.

The Bible says something better than both. It begins not with prohibitions but with a gift. God made us male and female, called his creation very good (Gen 1:31) and designed sexual union as a profound joining of husband and wife. Sex is not dirty or shameful. It is so precious that God has placed it within the protective boundaries of marriage, and so meaningful that it points beyond itself to Christ's love for his church (Eph 5:31-32).

This study tries to hold together truth and compassion. It speaks clearly about God's design, because God's design is good and his commands are for our flourishing. It speaks gently, because every reader is a sinner, many carry deep wounds, and some are wrestling with desires they did not choose. The gospel has good news for all of them.

Six units: (1) God's Good Design; (2) Purity in a Broken World; (3) The Gift of Singleness; (4) Same-Sex Attraction; (5) Male and Female He Created Them; (6) Healing, Forgiveness and Hope. It belongs with the studies on Christian Marriage, Biblical Manhood and Biblical Womanhood.

1.title: God's Good Design
1.overview:
Created male and female. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them (Gen 1:27). Our sex as male or female is not an accident or a social construction. It is part of how God made us, and both men and women equally bear his image. The difference between the sexes is not a problem to be overcome but a gift to be received.

Made for each other. In Genesis 2, God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him (Gen 2:18). Adam named the animals, but none was a fitting partner. Then God made the woman from the man and brought her to him. Adam's response was a song of delight: This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh (Gen 2:23). Man and woman are alike enough to be partners, and different enough to complement each other.

One flesh. Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh (Gen 2:24). Here is the pattern of marriage: leaving, holding fast, becoming one. Sexual union is the physical expression of a whole-life covenant. It joins two people at the deepest level, which is why it belongs only within marriage.

Without shame. And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed (Gen 2:25). Before the fall, there was perfect openness and trust. Sex was a delight without fear, guilt or exploitation.

Jesus affirms the design. When asked about divorce, Jesus went back to the beginning: Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female, and quoted Genesis 2:24 (Matt 19:4-5). For Jesus, God's creation design is the norm for marriage and sexuality.

Delight in marriage. The Bible is not embarrassed by sexual pleasure in marriage. Proverbs urges a husband, rejoice in the wife of your youth (Prov 5:18). The Song of Songs celebrates married love in poetry. Paul tells married couples not to deprive one another (1 Cor 7:3-5). God is the inventor of sexual joy.
1.theology:
The purposes of sex: Scripture shows several purposes for sexual union in marriage: union (one flesh), procreation (be fruitful and multiply, Gen 1:28), delight (Prov 5:18-19) and protection against temptation (1 Cor 7:2-5). These purposes belong together within the covenant of marriage.

A picture of Christ and the church: Paul quotes Genesis 2:24 and says, This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church (Eph 5:32). Marriage, including its sexual union, is a living picture of Christ's covenant love for his people. This is why God guards it so carefully.

The body matters: Christianity does not treat the body as unimportant. God made it, Christ took a body, the Spirit dwells in it and it will be raised. What we do with our bodies matters to God (1 Cor 6:13-14).
1.examples:
Then: In Eden, before sin, the first marriage was perfectly joyful. God himself brought the woman to the man, like a father walking his daughter down the aisle. Marriage was God's idea, and he was its first witness.

Now: A young Christian couple, both raised in churches that only spoke about sex as something to avoid, struggle with guilt in their marriage. Reading Genesis 2 and Proverbs 5 together, they realise that God is not embarrassed by their union. He designed it. Their shame begins to lift.

A simple test: Do you think of sexuality mainly as God's good gift or mainly as a problem? Scripture begins with the gift.

verseByVerse.quote: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them. And God blessed them. And God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Male and female together are the image of God. Neither alone tells the whole story. Then God blessed them and gave them a task: to be fruitful and multiply and to exercise dominion. Sexual difference is part of God's good creation and of his purpose for the world.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the LORD God said, "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him." Now out of the ground the LORD God had formed every beast of the field and every bird of the heavens and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. And whatever the man called every living creature, that was its name. The man gave names to all livestock and to the birds of the heavens and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper fit for him. So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and while he slept took one of his ribs and closed up its place with flesh. And the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man he made into a woman and brought her to the man. Then the man said, "This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man." Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh. And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The only thing in creation God called not good was the man's aloneness. God's answer was not another man but a woman, a fitting partner. The chapter ends with marriage defined: leaving, holding fast and becoming one flesh, without shame. Everything later in Scripture about sexuality builds on this foundation.

verseByVerse.quote: And Pharisees came up to him and tested him by asking, "Is it lawful to divorce one's wife for any cause?" He answered, "Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, 'Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh'? So they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisees asked about divorce, trying to trap Jesus. He took them back to creation. God made them male and female, and joined them in marriage. What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate. Marriage is not a human invention to be redefined at will. It is God's work.

verseByVerse.quote: Drink water from your own cistern, flowing water from your own well. Should your springs be scattered abroad, streams of water in the streets? Let them be for yourself alone, and not for strangers with you. Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth, a lovely deer, a graceful doe. Let her breasts fill you at all times with delight; be intoxicated always in her love. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The father warns his son against adultery, but not by making sex sound bad. He makes faithfulness sound wonderful. Drink water from your own cistern. Rejoice in the wife of your youth. Be intoxicated always in her love. The best protection against sexual sin is delight in God's good gift.

1.reflection:
What do Genesis 1 and 2 teach about why God made us male and female?

Why does sexual union belong only within marriage, according to Genesis 2:24?

How does Ephesians 5:31-32 deepen your understanding of marriage?

Has your view of sex been shaped more by culture, by shame or by Scripture?

2.title: Purity in a Broken World
2.overview:
The fall damaged every part of human life, including sexuality. Shame entered the garden (Gen 3:7). Since then, human sexuality has been marked by lust, exploitation, betrayal and confusion. Every person is affected.

God's will is our holiness. For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each one of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honor (1 Thess 4:3-4). Sexual immorality covers all sexual activity outside marriage between a man and a woman: sex before marriage, adultery, pornography and other sexual sins. Christians are called to purity in thought, word and deed.

Purity of heart. Jesus took the commandment against adultery to the heart: everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart (Matt 5:28). Purity is not only about what we do but about what we desire and dwell on. This is why pornography is so destructive. It trains the heart to treat people as objects, it fuels fantasy and it is often deeply addictive.

Your body belongs to the Lord. The body is not meant for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body (1 Cor 6:13). Paul argues that sexual sin is unique: it is a sin against one's own body (1 Cor 6:18). And for believers, the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit. You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body (1 Cor 6:19-20).

Marriage honoured. Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterous (Heb 13:4). Faithfulness within marriage, and chastity outside it, are both ways of honouring marriage.

Practical purity. For single people, purity means saving sex for marriage, and in dating, honouring the other person as a brother or sister in Christ. Living together before marriage, even without sex, puts people in the way of temptation and blurs the meaning of marriage. For married people, purity means faithfulness of body and heart, guarding against emotional affairs and treating one's spouse with honour. For all, it means wisdom with screens, friendships and situations.
2.theology:
Why "consent" is not enough: Our culture tends to treat consent as the only rule in sexual ethics. Consent is essential, and its absence makes sexual activity abuse. But God's design asks more than consent. It asks for covenant: a lifelong, exclusive promise in which sexual union expresses total self-giving.

Purity is not sinlessness: No one is perfectly pure. Every Christian has impure thoughts and desires to fight. Purity is a direction of life, not a flawless record, and it is pursued by grace.

The wider harm: Sexual sin harms not only individuals but families, children and communities. God's boundaries protect the vulnerable, especially women and children, from exploitation.
2.examples:
Then: The Corinthian church lived in a city known for sexual immorality, with temple prostitution and little restraint. Some believers argued that what they did with their bodies did not matter. Paul answered that the body is for the Lord and will be raised (1 Cor 6:12-20). Christian purity has always been countercultural.

Now: A Christian couple, engaged and planning their wedding, are told by friends that it is unrealistic not to live together first. They decide to wait. It is hard. But on their wedding day they have the joy of beginning their life together with nothing hidden and nothing regretted.

A simple test: What is the biggest threat to your sexual purity right now? What is one step you can take to guard against it?

verseByVerse.quote: For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each one of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honor, not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God; that no one transgress and wrong his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you. For God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness. Therefore whoever disregards this, disregards not man but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul is direct: God's will is your sanctification, and that includes sexual purity. Christians are not to act in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God. Sexual sin also wrongs others. And to reject this teaching is not to reject a human opinion but God himself, who gives his Holy Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? Never! Or do you not know that he who is joined to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For, as it is written, "The two will become one flesh." But he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him. Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Believers are members of Christ. Sexual union joins two people as one flesh, so sexual immorality joins a member of Christ to sin. Paul's command is short: Flee from sexual immorality. The motive is profound: your body is the temple of the Spirit, you were bought with a price, so glorify God in your body.

verseByVerse.quote: "You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.' But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart. If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body be thrown into hell. And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. For it is better that you lose one of your members than that your whole body go into hell. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus shows that God's law reaches the heart. Lustful looking is already adultery. Then he calls for radical action: whatever causes you to sin, cut it off. Purity requires both heart change and practical decisions about what we look at and where we go.

verseByVerse.quote: Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterous. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Marriage is to be held in honour by everyone, married and single. The marriage bed is to be kept pure. And there is a warning: God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterous. God takes sexual sin seriously because he takes marriage seriously.

2.reflection:
Why does Jesus say lust in the heart is already adultery?

What does it mean to "glorify God in your body" (1 Cor 6:20)?

What practical steps help you guard your purity in a culture saturated with sexual images?

How can your church help single and married people pursue purity without shame?

3.title: The Gift of Singleness
3.overview:
Many churches unintentionally treat singleness as a waiting room or a problem to be fixed. Yet Jesus was single. Paul was single. And Scripture speaks of singleness not as second best but as a good gift.

Paul's view. I wish that all were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another (1 Cor 7:7). Paul sees both marriage and singleness as gifts. He even says that singleness has particular advantages: the unmarried person can be anxious about the things of the Lord and serve him with undivided devotion (1 Cor 7:32-35).

Jesus' view. When the disciples suggested that it might be better not to marry, Jesus spoke of those who remain unmarried for the sake of the kingdom of heaven (Matt 19:12). Singleness for the sake of the kingdom is an honourable calling.

The future of marriage. Marriage is for this age. In the resurrection, they neither marry nor are given in marriage (Matt 22:30). The ultimate marriage is between Christ and his church. Single Christians already belong to that great marriage. Their lives point to the truth that human marriage is not the final goal of life.

The church as family. God promised eunuchs, who could have no children, a monument and a name better than sons and daughters (Isa 56:5). God settles the solitary in a home (Ps 68:6). Jesus said that whoever does the will of his Father is his brother and sister and mother (Mark 3:35). The church must be a real family for single people, including them in homes, holidays and leadership, not treating them as incomplete.

The struggles of singleness. Many singles did not choose singleness and long to be married. Their longing is not sinful. They may pray for a spouse. But they also face loneliness and sexual temptation without the outlet of marriage. They need honesty, friendship and support. Contentment is learned, not instant (Phil 4:11).
3.theology:
Is singleness a special gift only some have? Some read 1 Corinthians 7:7 as meaning that only those with a supernatural absence of sexual desire should remain single. More likely, Paul means that whatever state a person is in, married or single, is God's gift for that time. Singleness is a gift whenever God gives it, even when it is not wanted.

Not a lower calling: Some traditions have treated celibacy as spiritually higher than marriage; others treat marriage as the normal mark of maturity. Both are wrong. Each is a calling from God, with its own joys and burdens.

Wholeness in Christ: No one is incomplete because they are unmarried. And you have been filled in him (Col 2:10). Christ, not a spouse, is the source of our wholeness.
3.examples:
Then: Jesus lived as a single man, fully human and fully whole. He had deep friendships, including with Mary, Martha and Lazarus, whom he loved (John 11:5). His life shows that a single life can be full of love, friendship and purpose.

Now: A woman in her forties has never married and often feels invisible at church, where most events are for couples and families. A family in her church invites her to Sunday lunch every week. Their children call her "aunt." She mentors younger women and leads a Bible study. Her singleness has not been taken away, but it is no longer lonely.

A simple test: If you are married, which single person in your church could you include in your home this month?

verseByVerse.quote: I wish that all were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another. To the unmarried and the widows I say that it is good for them to remain single, as I am. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul wishes all could be single like him, but he recognises that each has his own gift from God. Marriage and singleness are both gifts. He tells the unmarried and widows that it is good for them to remain single, though not wrong to marry. Neither state is spiritually superior.

verseByVerse.quote: I want you to be free from anxieties. The unmarried man is anxious about the things of the Lord, how to please the Lord. But the married man is anxious about worldly things, how to please his wife, and his interests are divided. And the unmarried or betrothed woman is anxious about the things of the Lord, how to be holy in body and spirit. But the married woman is anxious about worldly things, how to please her husband. I say this for your own benefit, not to lay any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and to secure your undivided devotion to the Lord. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul explains the advantage of singleness: undivided devotion to the Lord. The married person rightly cares about pleasing a spouse; the single person can focus on the things of the Lord. Paul is not trying to restrict anyone, but to promote good order and devotion to Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely separate me from his people"; and let not the eunuch say, "Behold, I am a dry tree." For thus says the LORD: "To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant, I will give in my house and within my walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that shall not be cut off. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Eunuchs in Israel were excluded from parts of temple worship and could have no descendants. God promises those who keep his covenant a place in his house and a name better than sons and daughters, an everlasting name. In God's family, no one is left out because of their marital status.

verseByVerse.quote: The disciples said to him, "If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry." But he said to them, "Not everyone can receive this saying, but only those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who have been so from birth, and there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who is able to receive this receive it." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The disciples, shocked by Jesus' teaching on marriage, said it might be better not to marry. Jesus spoke of those who are single for different reasons, including those who choose singleness for the kingdom. Let the one who is able to receive this receive it. Singleness for Christ is an honourable path.

3.reflection:
How does your church treat single people? Are they fully part of the family?

What advantages of singleness does Paul describe in 1 Corinthians 7?

If you are single, how can you find contentment while honestly bringing your longings to God?

How does the truth that Christ is the true bridegroom shape our view of singleness and marriage?

4.title: Same-Sex Attraction
4.overview:
This is one of the most painful and debated questions facing the church today. It is not an abstract issue. It concerns real people, including Christians in our churches who experience same-sex attraction, often from a young age, and who did not choose it. They deserve both truth and love.

What Scripture says. The Bible consistently describes sexual relationships between people of the same sex as contrary to God's design. In the Law, it is forbidden (Lev 18:22). In Romans 1, Paul describes how humanity turned from the Creator, and how God gave people up to dishonorable passions, in which women and men exchanged natural relations for those that are contrary to nature (Rom 1:26-27). In 1 Corinthians 6:9-10, men who practise homosexuality are listed with the sexually immoral, adulterers, thieves and the greedy among those who will not inherit the kingdom. Every biblical reference to same-sex sexual activity is negative, and every biblical description of marriage is between a man and a woman.

Not a worse sin. Same-sex sexual activity is not singled out as uniquely terrible. In 1 Corinthians 6, it stands in a list with greed, drunkenness and slander. Christians who are proud of their own heterosexual purity while ignoring their greed or gossip have misunderstood the gospel.

Hope for all. Paul continues: And such were some of you. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God (1 Cor 6:11). The Corinthian church included people who had lived in every one of these sins. The gospel washed them.

Attraction and action. Experiencing same-sex attraction is a result of living in a fallen world, as all our disordered desires are. Feeling a temptation is not the same as sinning. A believer who experiences same-sex attraction and resists it out of love for Christ is walking faithfully. Their attractions may or may not change in this life. Some experience change, many do not. God does not promise that the desires will disappear, but he promises grace to live faithfully, and a future in which every desire will be made whole.

The church's calling. Churches must be places where believers who experience same-sex attraction can be honest without fear of rejection or gossip, where they find deep friendship and family, and where they are supported in faithfulness. Many such believers have chosen celibacy for Christ, often at great cost. They should be honoured, not pitied.
4.theology:
The views. Some Christians today argue that the biblical texts addressed only exploitative forms of same-sex activity, such as pederasty or temple prostitution, and that faithful, committed same-sex relationships are acceptable. The historic view of the church, in every tradition and century, is that same-sex sexual relationships are contrary to God's will.

The verdict: The historic view is right. Romans 1 grounds its teaching not in exploitation but in creation: the exchange of natural relations for what is contrary to nature. Jesus defined marriage by the creation pattern of male and female (Matt 19:4-6). And Scripture never presents any same-sex sexual relationship positively.

Identity: A Christian's deepest identity is not their sexual attractions but their union with Christ. Christians disagree over language, such as whether to describe oneself as a "gay Christian." It is wise to avoid language that suggests our desires define who we are. But all should speak with gentleness, remembering that every believer's desires are disordered in some way.

Coercion is wrong: Pressure, shaming or coercive programmes promising to change orientation have caused great harm. The church's task is to proclaim the gospel, call all to faithfulness and walk patiently with those who struggle.
4.examples:
Then: The church in Corinth was a mixed community of former idolaters, adulterers, thieves, drunkards and those who had practised homosexuality. Paul did not say they had to clean themselves up first. He said they had been washed. Their past did not define them; their Saviour did.

Now: A young man in a church youth group realises he is attracted to other young men. Terrified, he tells no one for years. Finally he confides in his pastor, expecting rejection. Instead his pastor thanks him for his trust, assures him of God's love, opens the Bible with him and promises to walk with him. He finds a few close friends in the church who know his story and support him. His struggle is real, but he is no longer alone.

A simple test: If someone in your church confided that they experience same-sex attraction, would they find in you both truth and love?

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves, because they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever! Amen. For this reason God gave them up to dishonorable passions. For their women exchanged natural relations for those that are contrary to nature; and the men likewise gave up natural relations with women and were consumed with passion for one another, men committing shameless acts with men and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul describes humanity's rebellion: exchanging the truth of God for a lie and worshipping creation rather than the Creator. God's judgment is to give people up to their desires. Same-sex relations are presented as one example of this deeper exchange. But Paul goes on to show that all are guilty (Rom 2-3). This passage is about all of us, before it is about anyone else.

verseByVerse.quote: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who practice homosexuality, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God. And such were some of you. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's list is broad: the sexually immoral, idolaters, adulterers, men who practise homosexuality, thieves, the greedy, drunkards, revilers and swindlers. No one is left out. But the passage turns on the word were. Such were some of you. Washed, sanctified, justified. The gospel offers a new identity to everyone, whatever their past.

verseByVerse.quote: Since then we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession. For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin. Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin. That means believers who experience same-sex attraction have a high priest who understands temptation. They can approach the throne of grace with confidence and find mercy and grace to help in time of need.

verseByVerse.quote: No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation he will also provide the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: No temptation is unique. God is faithful. He will provide a way of escape. This promise is for every believer, including those whose temptations are lifelong and hard. Faithfulness is possible, not by our strength, but by God's faithfulness.

4.reflection:
Why is it important that 1 Corinthians 6:9-10 lists many different sins together?

How would you explain the difference between same-sex attraction and same-sex sexual activity?

What can your church do to be a place of truth and love for believers who experience same-sex attraction?

How does 1 Corinthians 6:11 bring hope to every sinner, including you?

5.title: Male and Female He Created Them
5.overview:
Our culture increasingly teaches that a person's gender is determined by an inner sense of identity rather than by the body. Some people experience gender dysphoria, a deep and painful distress that their body does not match their sense of who they are. This is a real and often agonising experience, and those who face it deserve great compassion. But the Bible gives a different foundation for identity.

The body is a gift. God made us as embodied beings. For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made (Ps 139:13-14). Our bodies, including our sex, are not accidents to be overridden but part of God's good design. Being male or female is something we receive, not something we choose.

Living in a fallen world. Because of the fall, our bodies and minds do not always work as God designed. Some people are born with conditions in which physical sex is unclear. Some experience deep distress about their sex. These are not chosen, and they are not a reason for shame. They are part of the brokenness that affects all of creation (Rom 8:22-23).

Receiving our bodies. The Christian response to gender distress is not to reshape the body to fit the inner sense of self, but to seek healing and peace in receiving the body God has given, while walking patiently with the distress. This is hard and may take a lifetime. It requires deep pastoral care, wise counsel and a loving church family.

Distinctions that matter. In Scripture, men and women are not interchangeable (Deut 22:5; 1 Cor 11:14-15). Yet much of what our culture calls masculine or feminine is merely cultural. A gentle boy or an adventurous girl is not in the wrong body. Churches should avoid narrow stereotypes that make children feel they are not "real" boys or girls.

The hope of resurrection. Our bodies will be raised and transformed. We ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies (Rom 8:23). Every person who has struggled with their body has a hope: a body made whole.
5.theology:
The views. Some argue that gender identity, not the body, determines whether a person is a man or a woman, and that affirming a person's inner identity, including through medical transition, is the most loving response. The historic Christian view is that God gives our sex through our bodies, and that we are called to receive it.

The verdict: The historic view is right. Scripture grounds our identity as male or female in creation (Gen 1:27; Matt 19:4) and in the body (1 Cor 6:19-20). Altering the body to deny one's sex rejects the goodness of God's design. Yet compassion must govern how we speak. People with gender dysphoria are not projects to be fixed but people to be loved.

Children and teenagers: Parents and churches should respond to children's confusion with patience and love, not panic, avoiding both harsh reactions and quick affirmation of a changed identity. For some young people, distress eases over time.

Mercy toward those who have transitioned: People who have undergone transition and later come to Christ need a church that welcomes them, helps them walk forward faithfully and does not treat them with contempt.
5.examples:
Then: The Ethiopian eunuch was probably a man whose body had been altered, and who would have been excluded from the temple assembly (Deut 23:1). Yet Philip shared Christ with him and baptised him immediately (Acts 8:35-38). Isaiah's promise to eunuchs was fulfilled. Christ welcomes those whose bodies are marked by the brokenness of the world.

Now: A Christian family's teenage daughter tells them she believes she is a boy. Shocked, they want to react with anger. Instead, they listen, express their love and seek wise Christian counsel. They do not affirm a new identity, but they do not reject her. Over several years, with much prayer, patience and support, she comes to peace with her body. Her parents know other stories may end differently. They pray for every family facing this.

A simple test: When this subject comes up, is your first reaction anger, fear or compassion?

verseByVerse.quote: For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well. My frame was not hidden from you, when I was being made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth. Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David marvels at God's work in forming him in the womb. God knit him together, and every day of his life was written in God's book before any of them came to be. Our bodies are not random. They are crafted by God, with care and purpose. This is the foundation for receiving our bodies with gratitude.

verseByVerse.quote: Then God said, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth." So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God made humanity in his image, and made them male and female. The two sexes are woven into the account of humanity's creation. To be human is to be embodied as male or female. This is part of creation's original goodness, not a later imposition.

verseByVerse.quote: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us. For the creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the sons of God. For the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of him who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to corruption and obtain the freedom of the glory of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until now. And not only the creation, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies. For in this hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: All creation groans under the effects of the fall, and believers groan too, waiting for the redemption of their bodies. Paul is honest: the present is painful. But the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory to come. Those who struggle with their bodies share this groaning, and this hope.

verseByVerse.quote: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Believers are not their own, for they were bought with a price. These verses speak of sexual purity, but they also shape how we view our bodies: as gifts entrusted to us, to be used for God's glory, not as possessions to be reshaped at will.

5.reflection:
What does Psalm 139:13-16 teach you about your body?

How can Christians hold firmly to God's design while showing real compassion to those with gender dysphoria?

Which cultural stereotypes about masculinity and femininity are not actually biblical?

How does the hope of resurrection speak to those who struggle with their bodies?

6.title: Healing, Forgiveness and Hope
6.overview:
No one comes to this subject with clean hands. Every person reading this study has sinned sexually, in deed, in thought or both. Many have also been sinned against. The gospel is good news for the guilty and the wounded.

Forgiveness for the guilty. King David committed adultery and arranged a murder to cover it up. When he repented, God forgave him (2 Sam 12:13; Ps 51). A woman known in her town as a sinner washed Jesus' feet with her tears. Jesus said, Your sins are forgiven, and Your faith has saved you; go in peace (Luke 7:48, 50). There is no sexual sin that the blood of Christ cannot cleanse. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow (Isa 1:18).

Healing for the wounded. Sexual abuse is a horrific evil. Those who have been abused bear no guilt for what was done to them. The guilt belongs entirely to the abuser. Victims often carry deep shame that is not theirs to carry. Christ, who was himself stripped and shamed on the cross, understands. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds (Ps 147:3). Healing may take years, and wise counsel and medical help may be needed. But the God of all comfort is near. Any abuse must also be reported to the proper authorities.

New identity. In Christ, a person's past does not define them. Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come (2 Cor 5:17). The adulterer, the addict, the abuse survivor and the one who struggles with lifelong temptation are all invited to find their identity in Christ.

Rebuilding. After sexual sin, rebuilding trust in a marriage takes time, honesty and often outside help. After addiction, freedom involves accountability and practical change. After abuse, healing involves safety, truth and patient care. God's grace does not always erase consequences, but it is present in every stage of rebuilding.

The great wedding. Every human marriage, and every human longing for love, points to a greater reality: the marriage of Christ and his church. Let us rejoice and exult and give him the glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his Bride has made herself ready (Rev 19:7). Married or single, every believer is invited to that feast. There, every wound will be healed and every longing fulfilled.
6.theology:
Shame and guilt: Guilt is the objective fact of having sinned; shame is the feeling of being unclean or unworthy. Christ deals with both. He bears our guilt on the cross, and he removes our shame by clothing us in his righteousness (Isa 61:10).

Forgiveness does not remove all consequences: A forgiven adulterer may still face divorce; a forgiven abuser must still face the law. God's forgiveness is complete, but some earthly consequences remain. Grace is present even in them.

The church as a hospital: The church should be a place where sexual sin and sexual wounds can be confessed and healed, not hidden. This requires both clear teaching and deep compassion.
6.examples:
Then: Rahab was a prostitute in Jericho. She hid the Israelite spies and trusted in Israel's God. She was spared, joined God's people and became an ancestor of King David and of Jesus himself (Matt 1:5). Her past did not disqualify her from grace.

Now: A married man confesses to his wife that he has been viewing pornography for years. She is devastated. With the help of their pastor and a Christian counsellor, he takes practical steps toward freedom and accountability. It takes over a year for trust to begin to return. Today their marriage is stronger and more honest than it was before. They know it was grace.

A simple test: Is there a sexual sin or wound you have never brought to Christ? He is ready to forgive and heal.

verseByVerse.quote: One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, and he went into the Pharisee's house and reclined at table. And behold, a woman of the city, who was a sinner, when she learned that he was reclining at table in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster flask of ointment, and standing behind him at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment. Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him, for she is a sinner." And Jesus answering said to him, "Simon, I have something to say to you." And he answered, "Say it, Teacher." "A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they could not pay, he cancelled the debt of both. Now which of them will love him more?" Simon answered, "The one, I suppose, for whom he cancelled the larger debt." And he said to him, "You have judged rightly." Then turning toward the woman he said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not ceased to kiss my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment. Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little." And he said to her, "Your sins are forgiven." Then those who were at table with him began to say among themselves, "Who is this, who even forgives sins?" And he said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: A woman known as a sinner entered a Pharisee's house and wept over Jesus' feet. The Pharisee was scandalised. Jesus told a parable about two debtors and said that she loved much because she had been forgiven much. Then he spoke to her directly: your sins are forgiven; go in peace. Jesus welcomes the sexually broken.

verseByVerse.quote: Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause. "Come now, let us reason together, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God calls his people to wash themselves and to turn from evil. Then comes the great invitation: Come now, let us reason together. Though our sins are scarlet, they shall be white as snow. No stain is too deep for God to wash away.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and a song of praise is fitting. The LORD builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names. Great is our Lord, and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond measure. The LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked to the ground. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The God who determines the number of the stars and gives them names is the God who heals the brokenhearted. His greatness and his tenderness belong together. He lifts up the humble. Those wounded by sexual sin, their own or others', can bring their wounds to him.

verseByVerse.quote: Then I heard what seemed to be the voice of a great multitude, like the roar of many waters and like the sound of mighty peals of thunder, crying out, "Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns. Let us rejoice and exult and give him the glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his Bride has made herself ready; it was granted her to clothe herself with fine linen, bright and pure"—for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints. And the angel said to me, "Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb." And he said to me, "These are the true words of God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The great multitude praises God because the marriage of the Lamb has come. The Bride is clothed in fine linen, bright and pure, which is the righteous deeds of the saints. And there is a blessing for those invited. Every believer, married or single, will share in that wedding. It is the goal of all human love.

6.reflection:
What does Luke 7:36-50 teach about Jesus' response to sexual sinners?

How is the gospel good news for those who have been sexually abused?

What is the difference between guilt and shame? How does Christ deal with each?

How does the marriage of the Lamb give hope to married and single believers alike?
